title: IT Solution Architect / IT Inhouse Consultant – Microsoft (m/w/d)

title: Cloud Engineer
description: About the Role at RobCo RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works. We’re looking for a Cloud Engineer to join our Infrastructure & Data team as the fifth person in the team and become the go-to person for GitLab and GitOps best practices at RobCo. You’ll have a clear area to own from day one: shaping and improving the way we work with GitLab across engineering teams, with a strong focus on CI/CD, automation and scalable GitOps practices. You’ll also get exposure to Terraform, different cloud environments such as GCP and AWS, Kubernetes, MLOps and robot infrastructure. You’ll be working alongside teammates with deeper expertise in those areas, so there’s plenty of room to learn, broaden your technical scope and grow into new parts of the stack. Your Responsibilities Build and maintain GitOps workflows so that Git is the single source of truth for our infrastructure and application deployments. Manage promotion flows across environments (dev, production) and out to edge devices. Write and maintain Terraform (or similar IaC) for our AWS environment, delivered through pull requests, reviews, and automated pipelines. Build and improve CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI) that test, validate, and deploy changes safely. Help keep our platform reliable: set up monitoring, alerting, and dashboards, take part in incident response, and contribute to post-mortems. Apply software security best practices in your day-to-day work. Automate repetitive operational work and write small tools or services where they help. Support engineering teams with deployments, environment setup, and cost visibility. We're looking for someone who has: 3+ years of experience in a Cloud, DevOps, Platform, or Infrastructure engineering role. Hands-on experience with GitOps best practices. Experience building CI/CD pipelines. Familiar with infrastructure-as-code, ideally Terraform. Familiar with AWS, including EKS, RDS, S3, and EC2. Scripting or programming skills in Python, Go, or a similar language. A basic understanding of softwaresoftware security fundamentals and a willingness to deepen it. Nice to Have Basic knowledge of Kubernetes: deploying, operating, and troubleshooting workloads. Experience deploying to edge devices or managing fleets of distributed systems. Experience with secrets tooling (External Secrets, Sealed Secrets, Vault). Why join RobCo? Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation. Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time. As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work. Flat hierarchies, open communication, and regular 360° feedback enable fast decisions and support your professional and personal development. Wellpass membership (7,200+ studios across Germany), regular team events, and a team that takes both the work and the culture seriously. Flexible working hours, a modern office, and—depending on the role—the option to work from home. Regular team events—from relaxed beer & pizza nights on the rooftop terrace to shared experiences on ski trips or at Oktoberfest. About RobCo Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that adapts to your use case, improves over time, and requires zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model. We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. With $160M raised from investors including Lightspeed, Lingotto Innovation, and Sequoia, 200+ people globally, and 2.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our RobCo Bay Area Demo Lab in San Francisco. Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles. At RobCo, applicants are selected regardless of ethnic origin, religion, gender, age, disability, or sexual orientation. All decisions throughout the recruitment process are based solely on applicants’ qualifications, skills, knowledge, and experience, as well as relevant business requirements. title: Senior IT Analyst
description: About The Role The Senior IT Analyst is the principal in-house resource responsible for day-to-day IT support, providing first and second-line user support and day-to-day IT operations for approximately 80 users. As the principal person responsible for day-to-day IT operations, they will take ownership of incidents and service requests across the support lifecycle rather than operating solely as an escalation resource. This is a broad, senior analyst role for someone who is technically capable, comfortable working independently and able to manage competing priorities. The postholder will respond directly to users, resolve routine enquiries and requests, investigate more complex issues through to resolution and coordinate external technology suppliers where specialist expertise is needed. Alongside business-as-usual responsibilities, the role will support and deliver smaller technology projects and service improvements. By keeping FAIRR’s technology secure, reliable and easy to use, the role enables colleagues to focus on delivering FAIRR’s mission with investors and partners worldwide. Key Outcomes & Accountabilities OUTCOME 1: Users receive dependable, responsive IT support, with issues owned and resolved end to end Act as the principal in-house point of contact for day-to-day IT support, providing both first and second-line assistance according to operational needs. Resolve straightforward incidents and requests promptly, while taking the lead on more complex technical issues requiring deeper investigation and second-line expertise. Own and manage incidents and service requests from initial contact through to resolution, including access, software, equipment, permissions and non-standard user requirements, coordinating third-party suppliers or specialist support when required. Monitor recurring issues, identify root causes and implement practical improvements to reduce repeat incidents. Maintain accurate support records and produce clear information on service volumes, performance, trends and user experience. OUTCOME 2: Joiners, movers and leavers have the right access and equipment at the right time, and no more Coordinate all IT activities for joiners, movers and leavers in collaboration with HR and relevant managers. Create, amend and remove user accounts, licences, group memberships, permissions and application access accurately and on time, including removal of leaver access no later than the end of their last working day (or earlier where instructed by P&C). Prepare, issue, recover and securely manage laptops, mobile devices, peripherals and other IT equipment. Perform periodic access reviews and maintain appropriate evidence of approvals and completed actions. Manage shared, service and other non-person accounts, ensuring ownership, purpose and access are recorded. Where instructed by P&C or the Senior IT Manager, securely preserve or retrieve account and device data to support subject access requests, investigations or legal matters, maintaining confidentiality throughout. OUTCOME 3: IT changes are implemented in a controlled way with minimal disruption Plan, assess, document, communicate and implement routine IT changes in a controlled manner. Ensure changes have appropriate approvals, testing, implementation steps, back-out arrangements and post-change review where proportionate. Maintain the IT change schedule and coordinate activities to minimise disruption to users and business operations. Communicate planned changes clearly to affected users and stakeholders. Where changes need to take place outside normal working hours, schedule these in advance with the Senior IT Manager’s agreement (see Section 8). OUTCOME 4: IT services and workplace technology operate reliably and are used effectively and securely Administer Microsoft 365 and other cloud applications used by the organisation, including routine configuration, licence and user administration. Support laptops, mobile devices, meeting-room technology, printers, connectivity and standard workplace applications. Coordinate hardware repairs, replacements, warranty cases, software renewals and operational supplier activities. Maintain user guides, knowledge articles, standard operating procedures and support documentation. Provide practical guidance and training that helps users make effective and secure use of technology. OUTCOME 5: IT records, controls and evidence are complete, current and audit-ready Maintain complete and accurate asset, software, licence, supplier and other operational IT registers. Record equipment allocation, ownership, status, location, lifecycle and disposal information, and perform periodic reconciliations. Follow and help maintain IT policies, standards, procedures and control evidence. Complete routine operational checks and scheduled control activities, escalating risks, exceptions or control failures promptly. Support audits, reviews and compliance activities by providing accurate records and evidence. Handle devices, accounts and information in line with security, privacy and records-management requirements. Support compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 (as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025), including immediately escalating any suspected personal data breach to the Data Protection Lead so that the organisation can meet the 72-hour ICO reporting deadline where applicable. OUTCOME 6: Small projects and improvements are delivered and technology keeps getting better Deliver or support small IT projects, upgrades, application roll-outs and service improvements. Gather requirements, coordinate suppliers, plan user communications, support testing and manage implementation activities. Identify opportunities to improve reliability, security, efficiency and the user experience. Keep project actions, risks, decisions, documentation and handover materials up to date. Success Measures Success in the role will be assessed through: Service delivery Users receive dependable and responsive first and second-line technical support, with routine and complex issues resolved effectively. Incidents and requests are responded to and resolved within agreed service levels. User satisfaction with IT support is consistently positive. Accuracy, security and control Incidents, requests, access changes and joiner, mover and leaver activities are completed accurately and on time. 100% of leaver accounts disabled by the end of the last working day; new joiners fully equipped and set up on day one. Operational records, registers and control evidence are complete, current and reliable. Periodic access reviews and asset reconciliations completed on schedule with no significant audit findings. Change and improvement Changes and small projects are delivered in a controlled way with minimal disruption. Recurring problems are reduced and practical improvements are implemented continuously. Feedback from the Senior IT Manager, colleagues and suppliers on collaboration, communication and ownership. Technical Expertise & Role-Specific Capability Essential Strong hands-on experience providing both first and second-line IT support within a modern workplace environment, with particular strength in diagnosing and resolving more complex technical issues. Demonstrable experience managing a broad range of incidents and service requests through their full lifecycle, from initial user contact to resolution. Practical experience of joiner, mover and leaver processes, identity administration, permissions and access control. Experience administering Microsoft 365 and supporting Windows devices, laptops, mobile devices and common business applications. Experience maintaining IT asset records, operational registers, procedures and control evidence. Understanding of proportionate change management, information security and data protection practices. Ability to troubleshoot methodically, make sound decisions and know when to engage specialist support. Experience coordinating external IT suppliers and seeing actions through to completion. Ability to organise a varied workload independently and balance urgent support needs with planned operational work. Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical matters to non-technical users. Experience contributing to or delivering small IT projects and technology changes. Desirable Experience in a small organisation where the role covers a broad range of operational IT responsibilities. Working knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, Autopilot, SharePoint and Teams administration. Experience with IT service management tools and ITIL-aligned working practices. Experience supporting SaaS applications and coordinating managed service, cyber security or other specialist partners. Relevant technical or service management certification (e.g. Microsoft 365 / Azure certifications, ITIL Foundation), or equivalent practical experience. Career Framework Expectations Our Career Framework provides a shared approach to development and performance across the organisation. It is built around four core pillars: Connect, Deliver, Focus and Lead, which outline the key behaviours and expectations expected at all levels. In this role, the pillars look like this: CONNECT — Building trust, relationships and collaboration Collaborative and able to build effective relationships with users, colleagues and suppliers. Technically credible, user-focused and committed to providing a high-quality service. DELIVER — Driving outcomes and execution Proactive and self-sufficient, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. Calm and organised when handling competing priorities or service disruption. FOCUS — Applying expertise and driving improvement Detail-oriented and disciplined about keeping records, documentation and actions up to date. Curious and improvement-minded, with a willingness to learn and adapt. LEAD — Leading self, others and organisational success Practical and proportionate, applying appropriate control without unnecessary bureaucracy. Role-models secure and responsible use of technology and shares knowledge so colleagues become more self-sufficient. Organisational Values We are change makers: keeps the technology behind FAIRR’s work dependable, so colleagues can spend their time on the mission rather than on IT problems. We collaborate: works closely with HR, managers, colleagues and suppliers to deliver a joined-up service. We innovate: looks for better, simpler and more secure ways of working, and delivers improvements that last. We act with integrity: handles privileged access, devices and personal data responsibly, confidentially and transparently. Additional Information Working Arrangements Hybrid working from near Marble Arch (Oxford Street), London, UK, in line with FAIRR’s organisational working arrangements. Normal working hours are 9.00am–5.30pm, Monday to Friday. Because much of the role is hands-on (devices, meeting-room technology, joiner set-up), the postholder will be expected to work on site at least 3 days per week and on key operational days such as new starter inductions. Occasional work outside normal hours may be required for planned changes or urgent incidents. This will be agreed in advance wherever possible and recognised through time off in lieu in line with FAIRR policy. Travel Requirements Occasional travel within London and the UK may be required (e.g. supplier visits, training or events). International travel is not an expected part of the role. Salary Range To be confirmed during recruitment stage. Benefits Benefits will be provided in line with FAIRR’s standard employee benefits package. If you're results-driven and want a fast-growing company with strong growth and earnings potential, apply today! Much of our operation runs on software we build ourselves. Thank you! #LI-HybridDowners Grove, IL About Roadrunner Roadrunner is for ambitious, smart people who excel at execution over talking about it, and who would rather invent the next standard in freight than accept the status quo. We are looking for the Best of the Best. Action driven leaders who want to be part of real change and help design the future of LTL in the U.S. This is a place where high performers can grow, influence outcomes, and make an impact while working directly with executives and smart people from across industries. We bring a winner mindset. We take ownership, raise the bar, and measure ourselves by results. We Run Safe. We Run Smart. We Run Together. These principles create an environment of high standards, clear ownership, and direct collaboration. We trust data over intuition, move with urgency, and hold each other accountable because winning requires it. Roadrunner exists to prove that LTL can be better than the industry has settled for. To be the best means we need to think bigger, look outside the box, and question every assumption: too many handoffs, limited visibility, and the quiet belief that “this is just how it works.” We rejected that story. We built a proprietary Smart Network™ for direct, long haul, metro to metro service that delivers fewer touches, faster transit, real time visibility, and genuine accountability. We are the most tech forward company in LTL, and we are not finished widening the gap. The foundation is already strong. Recognized as one of Built In Chicago’s Best Large Places to Work. Earning top marks for improvement, quality, and service. The real opportunity is still ahead: helping invent what comes next. If you want to be evaluated among the Best of the Best and help set the new standard in LTL, we should talk.
